message.content:
Below are two ways you can create a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS:

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# 1️⃣  Set your project and zone
PROJECT_ID="your-project-id"
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# 2️⃣  Create a new instance
gcloud compute instances create "rtx-a6000-ubuntu" \
  --project="${PROJECT_ID}" \
  --zone="${ZONE}" \
  --machine-type="n1-standard-8" \          # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM
  --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1" \
  --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \
  --image-project="ubuntu-os-cloud" \
  --boot-disk-size="100GB" \
  --boot-disk-type="pd-ssd" \
  --maintenance-policy="TERMINATE" \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional
```

**Explanation of key flags**

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU & memory allocation. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs and 30 GB RAM. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the GPU. `nvidia-tesla-a6000` is the RTX A6000. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Selects Ubuntu 20.04 LTS. |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk of 100 GB. |
| `--maintenance-policy` | `TERMINATE` means the VM will be stopped if the host is rebooted. |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Automatically restarts the VM if it crashes. |

> **Tip:** If you need more vCPUs or RAM, adjust `--machine-type` accordingly. For example, `n1-highmem-16` gives 16 vCPUs and 104 GB RAM.

---

## 2. Using the REST API (JSON)

If you prefer to use the REST API directly (e.g., from a script or a custom application), you can POST a JSON payload to the Compute Engine API.

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/your-project-id/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/your-project-id/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470"
      }
    ]
  },
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "TERMINATE",
    "automaticRestart": true
  }
}
```

**How to send the request**

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/your-project-id/zones/us-central1-a/instances"
```

Replace:

- `your-project-id` with your actual GCP project ID.
- `instance.json` with the path to the JSON file containing the payload above.

---

### Quick Checklist

- **Project & Zone** – Ensure you’re targeting the correct project and zone (`us-central1-a` is a common choice for GPU availability).
- **GPU Availability** – Check that the RTX A6000 is available in your chosen zone. You can list available GPUs with:
  ```bash
  gcloud compute accelerator-types list --zone us-central1-a
  ```
- **Billing** – GPU instances incur additional costs. Verify that billing is enabled for your project.
- **Permissions** – The service account used must have the `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` role (or equivalent) to create instances.

Feel free to tweak the machine type, disk size, or other parameters to fit your workload!
